string-array.name: privacy_stays
string-array.item: There is no account and no Glovebox server. Your vehicles, service records, photos, documents and settings exist only on this phone.
The database, photos and documents are encrypted with keys held by Android Keystore.

Documents open inside Glovebox. A PDF is drawn by a part of the app that runs walled off from the rest, with no network and no files of its own, and it is read from memory, not from a copy on the phone.
Android\'s own cloud backup and device-to-device transfer are switched off for this app. The only copy that can leave is a backup file you make yourself.
The home-screen widget is off unless you switch it on in Notifications. While it is on, your vehicles\' names and their next service show on the home screen without unlocking Glovebox.

resources.string: What is sent, and to whom

string-array.name: privacy_sent
string-array.item: The app talks to one organisation: NHTSA, the U.S. vehicle safety agency (vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov and api.nhtsa.gov).
Decoding a VIN sends that VIN.
Adding a vehicle without a VIN asks for NHTSA\'s list of makes, then for the models of the make and year you pick.
Checking for recalls sends the year, make and model. It does not send the VIN.
Like any website, NHTSA can see the internet address the request came from.
Nothing else is sent: no mileage, records, photos, documents, names, license plate or location.

string-array.name: privacy_never
string-array.item: No analytics, crash reporting, advertising or tracking, and no third-party code that reports back to anyone.

string-array.name: privacy_saved
string-array.item: A backup file is encrypted with the password you choose. Glovebox does not keep the password and cannot recover it.
A PDF or Markdown export is not encrypted. Anyone who has the file can read it.

A schedule, milestone table or set of torque specs saved as an import file is not encrypted either. It holds what is on that screen (items and intervals, mileages and jobs, or fasteners with your values and notes) and nothing else about your vehicle or its history.
Deleting all data in Settings does not touch files you have already saved elsewhere.

string-array.name: privacy_imported
string-array.item: Import reads the one file you pick, on this phone, and adds what it holds to the vehicle you choose. A Carfax report PDF is read the same way, for its service visits. The file is not copied or kept unless you tick \"Keep a copy in this vehicle\'s documents\", and nothing is sent anywhere.

string-array.name: privacy_leaving
string-array.item: A manufacturer\'s recall page, a maker\'s manual or guide, Find a dealer, the source code and any link you tap in a PDF open in your browser or maps app. What those do is up to them.
Opening a document in another app, sharing a document or photo, or saving a file hands a copy to the app you choose.

string-array.name: privacy_permissions
string-array.item: Camera: to scan a VIN from its barcode or from print, to read the odometer off the dash, and to photograph receipts, parts and paperwork. Scanner and dash frames are read on this phone and thrown away, never stored or sent.
Notifications: for reminders, new recalls and the backup reminder.
Internet: for NHTSA only.
Fingerprint, face or screen lock: Android does the checking and tells the app only whether it passed.

string-array.name: privacy_updates
string-array.item: Glovebox does not check for updates itself. If you installed it with Obtainium, Obtainium checks GitHub for new releases.
